blindComparison: No blind comparison was performed. Source identities are known. These results do not change any concept-element judgment.
verdictScope: The recorded stale examine state is absent after the three previously reproduced death-recovery routes. Normal examine/conversation completion and cancellation without end effects pass the bounded actual-source CPU checks. This applies to the pinned uncommitted repair source, not to an unmeasured built or deployed game.
sourceState: Live uncommitted repair was pinned before execution; all 40 actual source/style files in its manifest still match the live workspace at final review. The extra package.json only enables isolated ESM loading.

resolved.symptom: An authored cellar examine text and its advance callback survived natural gas death and GET UP, TITLE → NEW GAME or TITLE → CONTINUE.
resolved.repair: Death and resetWorld call non-committing Director.cancelDialogue; the runner clears active conversation state/listeners without finish; UI hide clears text, typing, choices and callbacks, and hidden box taps return immediately.
resolved.measuredResult: All three actual recovery flows now hide and clear the prior reading already at death, return to PLAY/alive without the stale text, and ignore the old hidden box taps and typing update. The normal authored five-paragraph examine still completes in 10 taps.
resolved.mechanismScope: Confirmed for the actual source state/callback lifecycle. No rendered overlay or native pointer behavior was measured.

names: Authored vent decision still commits the chosen effect and ends through real UI callbacks
Cancellation before a choice does not select it; delayed release on its removed node is inert while hidden
Diagnostic onEnd effects and callback distinguish cancel from ordinary completion

measured: The actual Game interaction target selects the unlocked cellar door and authored cellar_floor examine after real interior collision movement. Health and initial gas saturation were not edited.

Full Game/Actor/Lungs simulation produces natural gas death after 49.18333333333174 seconds of reading. The existing 1400 ms death callback is delivered by a deterministic timer fixture; this is not a wall-clock measurement.

The actual title/death/pause button callback bindings and source-extracted main start/continue closures perform the three recovery routes. The continue scenario uses the actual SAVE button before entry; later authored autosave may replace that snapshot.

Authored vent-choice completion still commits its chosen effect and actual gas consequence, then returns to PLAY through the normal UI callbacks. Already committed choice effects survive cancellation.

Diagnostic onEnd effects and callback counters distinguish cancel from finish: cancellation produces zero end effects/callbacks, ordinary completion produces exactly one, and repeated finish is inert.
Cancellation stops the actual talking NPC action and clears pending trade. Both resetWorld and death use the shared cleanup.
The separate refuter confirms normal completion still performs its NPC met, quest notification and save effects, while cancellation does not perform them.

observations.area: Artificial detached choice callback delivery after replacement conversation
observations.result: The independent minimal DOM can force an old detached choice listener to reach a replacement onChoose. Native capture, disconnected-node retargeting and trusted delivery are absent. The lost-capture control prevents the forced action.
observations.disposition: Browser reachability is not measured; no product finding is asserted from this fixture-only delivery. This review does not claim arbitrary retained callback references are guarded across all future conversations.

limitations: No browser, local server, socket, Appium, Simulator, rendered frame or trusted/physical smartphone action was executed.
The starting outdoor position is staged at the authored cellar exterior without changing health, gas, items or progression. The full outdoor walk from the initial spawn is outside this scope.
The minimal DOM has no CSS/layout, native pointer capture or hit testing. Menus panel contents, canvas drawing, input acquisition and wall-clock timers are fixtures.
Diagnostic conversations are test-only controls, not authored product story content or quality evidence.

The three recovery paths are measured end to end at CPU boundaries; additional no-save retry is supported by the shared death cleanup and direct lifecycle checks, not a new end-to-end r3 browser measurement.
The earlier r1 failing evidence and r2 failed Sol-approach setup remain intact. Neither is overwritten or represented as a repaired-build browser result.
Existing product quality/element judgments remain unchanged; current-build smartphone and blind comparisons are separate work.
